battle.name: 彭孝才起義
battle.brief: 大業九年（613年）二月，泗水北岸彭城郡治一帶，首領彭孝才聚眾起兵反隋，與同年山東、河北、江淮多處起義相應；此役在同年內被隋廷郡兵鎮壓。卡面的羅馬短劍不在此役現場，泗水城牆下見血的是環首刀、削尖竹槊與官軍的長槊步弩；短劍所代表的刺突節奏，正是近身格鬥的核心。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 這場衝突是隋朝大業九年（613年）彭城一帶的農民起義，對手是隋廷在淮北的州郡官署與鎮壓部隊。起義方沒有國號，也沒有常備建制，而是以彭城為中心、由逃戶、潰卒、僮僕與被強徵丁男拼成的武裝集團，首領彭孝才自彭城聚眾起兵，兵眾多為鄉里部曲，既無可考的將領編號，也沒有成建制的後勤。正面對手是隋朝的州郡體系：彭城郡治所在城池由郡丞與縣令據守，郡兵、州兵、縣兵是常備骨幹，其餘靠臨時徵發的鄉里丁男與民間武裝充數。鎮壓這類亂事最高層的指揮權在河南道行台，行台自洛陽調兵策應；而正在遼東攻打高句麗的煬帝不可能回師，江淮一線的任務因此落到地方郡兵與臨時派遣的武賲郎將、騎兵身上。雙方真正的差距不在訓練，而在組織與補給：隋軍有城、有兵器、有官倉，義軍只有鄉里之間的臨時結合。戰爭的實質，是隋朝把全部精銳押在遼東戰線之後，江淮腹地只剩下薄薄的一層地方兵。
countriesEn: This conflict was a peasant rising in the Pengcheng area during the ninth year of the Daye era (613), fought against the Sui state's prefectural and county administration in northern Huai and the troops it used to suppress the revolt. The insurgents had no state title and no standing establishment; they were an armed mass gathered at Pengcheng out of absentees, deserters, household servants and conscripted labouring men, led by Peng Xiaocai, and their numbers came mostly from local neighbourhood companies, with no recorded officer structure and no organised logistics. The opposing side was the machinery of the Sui prefectures and counties: the walled seat of Pengcheng commandery was held by the assistant prefect and the magistrate, and the backbone of its garrison was made up of commandery, prefecture and county levies, supplemented by hastily summoned village militia and locally raised armed men. The highest authority for crushing such disorder lay with the Henan Circuit headquarters, which coordinated the response out of Luoyang; the emperor himself was in Liaodong fighting Goguryeo and could not return, so the task in the Huai lands fell by default to the county troops of the localities and to imperial guards and cavalry detached for the occasion. The gap between the two sides lay not in drill but in organisation and supply: the Sui possessed walls, arsenals and public granaries, while the rebels possessed nothing but a temporary union formed between neighbouring villages. The real substance of the fight was that, with the whole elite of the dynasty committed to the Liaodong front, the interior of the Huai region was left covered by a single thin layer of local troops.
people: 彭孝才是這場起義唯一能夠確定的首領姓名，其餘人物多數只以官職或兵種出現。關於他的記載極短，只說他大業九年在彭城起兵、兵鋒指向郡治；他的籍貫細節、年齡與所部人數，正史都沒有交代，後世史家多依《隋書》與《資治通鑑》兩書的簡筆，定其為彭城一帶的亂首，與他同時被記錄的還有山東長平的王薄題反詩聚眾、鄒縣的孫安祖、河北唐縣的宋子賢、濟北長白山的杜伏威、徽州歙縣的劉元進、浙西信安的陳瑱、東郡的呂明星、齊郡平原有郝孝德，另有劉道支、劉君朗等名號。隋煬帝楊廣是這一片亂局的中心人物：他自大業八年起兩次征高句麗，兵丁與府庫都壓在遼東，班師之後又北巡、代州巡邊，把江淮的丁男一批批抽走，被抽走的人正是各地起義的兵源。鎮壓一線的指揮官，隋書多以武賲郎將、果毅、校尉之類的名號帶過，未留下可以核對的個人名；被記下名字的，多是後來在新王朝中成器者。
peopleEn: Peng Xiaocai is the only name that can be attached with certainty to this rising; nearly everyone else appears only by office or by type of troops. The record about him is extremely short, stating only that he rose at Pengcheng in the ninth year of Daye and pointed his men at the commandery seat; the details of his origin, his age and the size of his following are not recorded by the official histories, and later historians take their line from the brief notices in the History of Sui and the Comprehensive Mirror, treating him as a local rebel chief of the Pengcheng area. Alongside him, this year produced Wang Bo, who posted seditious verses and drew a crowd at Changping in Shandong, Sun Anzu at Zou county, Song Zixian at Tang county in Hebei, Du Fuwei on Changbai Mountain north of Jibei, Liu Yuanjin at She county in Huizhou, Chen Zhen at Xinan in western Zhejiang, Lü Mingxing at Dongjun, and Hao Xiaode on the plains of Qijun, together with such names as Liu Daozhi and Liu Junlang. Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, was the hub of this whole field of disorder: from the eighth year of Daye he had campaigned against Goguryeo twice, and the manpower and the granaries of the empire were both committed in the northeast; after the withdrawal he toured the north and marched through Dai prefecture, and each circuit drew another batch of men out of the Huai region, and those men drawn out were precisely the source of the manpower for these risings. The commanders on the suppression side are mostly passed over in the History of Sui as guards officers, commandants and colonels, and no individual name survives there that can be checked against anything else; the names that were written down are largely men who later rose to office under the new dynasty.
kits: 卡面上這件兵器是羅馬短劍，出自公元前一世紀前後的羅馬兵工場：寬闊的雙刃劍身、短小的握柄、球形護手，設計的出發點不是揮砍而是刺，羅馬人靠一邊執盾、一邊捅刺的節奏去吃掉對面的陣線。但短劍並不存在於此役。彭城在淮河北岸，與地中海世界沒有任何往來，這場起義裡沒有任何一位羅馬兵。真正在泗水流域的城牆下動手的，是漢晉以來一直沿用的環首刀與直刃刀，以及削尖的竹木長桿；隋軍的標準配備是明光鎧甲、長槊與步弩，騎兵用環首刀，弓弩手配擲矛與蹶張弩，郡兵則多為各縣的土兵。義軍這一邊更簡陋：農具改成的叉與鋤、柴刀、削尖的竹桿，以及從高句麗戰線逃回的潰卒帶回的殘缺甲片。若要在兵學上找對應，卡面短劍提示的正是此役真正決定勝負的那件事——近身之後怎麼把刀捅進去。隋軍靠長槊先手、靠環首刀收尾，義軍在失去長兵器後只剩刀與矛，因此每一次貼身都短促而兇狠。短劍的另一個教訓是：任何單手直刃武器，若沒有配套的盾牌與腰身支撐，刺擊的力道並不比斬擊更省力。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a Roman gladius, produced in the legionary workshops of the first century BC: a broad double-edged blade, a short grip, a globular pommel, designed not for the cut but for the thrust, since the Romans closed with the line by holding the shield in one hand and stabbing in a measured rhythm with the other. But the gladius has no place here. Pengcheng stood on the north bank of the Sishui with no contact whatsoever with the Mediterranean world, and not one Roman soldier served in this rising. What actually swung steel below the Sishui was the ring-pommel and straight single-edged blade carried in China since the Han and Jin dynasties, together with poles sharpened from bamboo and wood. The standard Sui kit was bright armour, long spears and crossbows for the foot, ring-pommel sabres for the cavalry, throwing javelins and powerful tension bows for the missile troops, while the county levies were largely local soil-soldiers with whatever they owned. The rebel side was poorer still: farm tools converted into forks and hoes, woodcutters' blades, poles sharpened to a point, and the broken fragments of armour carried back by deserters from the Goguryeo front. If the gladius is read as a parallel in military art, it points at the one thing that actually decided this engagement: what happens when the fighting closes to arm's length and the blade has to go in. The Sui answered that with the long spear first and the ring-pommel sabre last; the rebels, deprived of reach, had only knife and point, so every close encounter was short and vicious. The second lesson of the gladius is that a single-edged straight weapon, unsupported by a shield and by the bracing of the body, gains nothing by choosing the thrust over the cut.
tactics: 起義能夠成形，靠的是鄉里網絡而不是陣法。彭孝才在彭城聚眾後，能沿泗水與舊驛道把相鄰幾個鄉里拉進來：農忙與徵役的時候，隊伍靠口耳相傳在村莊之間流動；一旦郡兵離城追擊，這些人就散回田間、廢舍與水網地帶，官軍一過，隊伍又重新聚合。進攻方式是密集的鄉里人群倚靠村莊與堤埂作遮蔽，短兵相接時用削尖的竹木與柴刀硬打，缺少任何可與官軍步兵方陣相持的縱深。隋軍這邊恰恰相反：郡兵依托城池結陣，出城時以武賲與精騎為前驅，步卒在後列弩、列槊，器械與糧秣靠郡兵護衛的運糧隊從後方州縣接續。泗水是這條補給線的骨幹，從淮濱與宿州方向運來的糧秣和徵發的丁男都沿水路北上，因此控制水路、封鎖渡口是官軍最省力的辦法。義軍一旦被逼離鄉里、失去糧食與人丁補充，就只能退入山澤或散為流寇，這也是隋末多數早期起義很快收束的原因。
tacticsEn: What allowed the rising to take shape was the network of neighbourhoods rather than any formation. Once Peng Xiaocai had gathered a crowd at Pengcheng he could pull in the adjoining villages along the Sishui and the old post road: at planting and at conscription time the columns moved from hamlet to hamlet by word of mouth; once the county troops left the city in pursuit, these men dispersed back into the fields, the abandoned houses and the marshy ground, and when the government columns had passed, the crowd re-formed. The mode of attack was a dense mass of villagers using the hamlets and the embankments as cover, fighting at close quarters with sharpened poles and woodcutters' blades, with no depth that could stand against a Sui infantry line. The Sui worked the opposite way: the county troops formed up on the walls, and when they came out the imperial guards and picked cavalry led, with the foot closed up behind them, spears and crossbows ranked in order, while the baggage and the rations were carried forward by supply trains guarded by the same county troops. The Sishui was the backbone of that supply line: grain and conscripted labour came up from the Huai bend and from Su prefecture by water, so controlling the river and closing the crossings was the cheapest thing the government could do. Once the rebels were driven away from their villages and cut off from food and from new recruits, they could only fall back into the hills or dissolve into bands of roving bandits, and that is why most of the early Sui uprisings closed so quickly.
data: 關於這場起義本身的數字，正史留下的極少，能夠核對的只有年份、地點，以及它在大業九年全國亂局中的位置，其餘只能從同期全局的量級去框定。大業八年第一次征高句麗，隋廷發兵百十三萬、號稱二百萬，《資治通鑑》記其歸還遼東時存者僅二千七百人；大業九年再發大軍征遼，同樣是百萬之眾，至平壤而不能下，士卒死傷與疫癘極為慘烈，府庫因供應軍糧而空竭。府兵舊制在這時已漸虛，郡兵、州兵與臨時募兵才是實際戰力。彭孝才這類起義的兵源正來自這兩次抽調：編戶齊民、逃戶、潰卒與僮僕混雜其中。至於起義本身的確切人數、攻城器械數與戰損，正史沒有留下可用的數目。同期可對照的只有規模量級：王薄旬日之間聚眾數萬，郝孝德聚眾數萬，杜伏威在長白山初起時人數有限，才得以保存實力。地理距離也有明確量度：彭城距東都洛陽直線近千里，泗水自彭城向西北入淮，向下可達運河北段的漕渠，義軍不必遠行就能取得水路上的補給。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this rising itself. The official histories leave little more than the year, the place, and its position within the general collapse of the ninth year of Daye, and everything else can only be framed by the scale of the wider conflict. In the first Goguryeo campaign of the eighth year of Daye the Sui court called up 1,130,000 men and announced the host as two million, and the Comprehensive Mirror records that when the army came back to Liaodong only 2,700 men were left. The following year a second host of the same order was raised for the campaign in Liaodong; it advanced to Pyongyang without taking it, and the losses of men and the epidemics in the army were appalling, while the treasury was emptied by the cost of feeding it. The old fubing establishment had by now become hollow, and the county and prefecture levies together with hastily raised recruits were the real strength in the field. The manpower of risings like Peng Xiaocai's came precisely from these two levies: registered households, absentees, deserters and household servants were all mixed into them. As for the size of this particular force, the number of siege implements and the casualties, the official histories leave no usable figures. The only usable comparison is the scale of comparable risings in the same year: Wang Bo drew tens of thousands within days of posting his verses, Hao Xiaode gathered tens of thousands, while Du Fuwei at Changbai Mountain began with few enough men to preserve his force. Distance is also measurable: Pengcheng lies nearly a thousand li in a straight line from the eastern capital Luoyang, and the Sishui runs from Pengcheng north-westward into the Huai and downward to the canal that carried the northern grain traffic, so the rebels could draw on the river's supplies without travelling far.
cause: 為什麼起義會在彭城爆發，可以從三條線索推。一是兵：兩次征高句麗一共抽走數百萬丁男，府兵與郡兵被一批批調離，戰敗者的遺散與潰逃者散回鄉里，其中相當一部分帶著繳獲的甲兵與裝備回到原籍，這是任何起義最現成的武裝來源。二是役：隋廷北巡、代州巡邊與江都巡幸所徵的力役從未停止，泗水一線的漕丁、渡夫、推車人年年被拉去打仗，農時失耕。三是糧：兩次征遼的軍糧沿泗水、汴水與洛陽的官倉周轉，江淮的常平倉被調空，糧價隨之上揚，泗水兩岸的縣份最先感覺到飢餓。彭城是南北漕運與驛道的交會點，往來的人與消息密集，一句號召就能在幾個鄉里之間傳開。於是本地的飢民、逃兵與被逼到極處的丁男聚到彭城城郊，把原本只是搶掠與私鬥的事態，變成一場對郡縣的公開挑戰。
causeEn: Why the rising broke out at Pengcheng can be reconstructed along three lines. The first is men. The two Goguryeo campaigns drew away millions of conscripts, and the households of the Sishui valley were emptied in the process; the survivors and the deserters drifted home again, and some of them brought back captured armour and weapons, which is the most ready-made source of armament any rising has. The second is labour. The northern tours, the march through Dai prefecture and the imperial progresses to Jiangdu never stopped taking porters, ferrymen and carters from the Sishui line, and the ploughing season was lost every year. The third is grain. The army rations for the Liaodong campaigns moved along the Sishui, the Bian water and the public granaries of Luoyang, and the ever-present stores of the Huai region were emptied to feed them, so prices rose and the counties along the Sishui were the first to feel the hunger. Pengcheng was a junction of the north-south grain traffic and the post road, so people and news moved through it thickly, and a single summons could pass from one neighbourhood to the next. Men who were hungry, men who were deserters and men driven to the end by conscription therefore gathered outside the walls of Pengcheng, turning what had been private robbery and local quarrel into an open challenge to the commanderies and counties.
impact: 單看彭孝才起義本身，它在大業九年之內就被鎮壓，規模有限，沒有改變任何政權的歸屬；但放在隋末的全局裡，它是壓力計上的第一個刻度。這一年被記錄在案的起義遍佈山東、河北、河南、江南與東南，隋廷的郡兵在同一時間被拉向十幾個方向，結果是沒有一個方向能投入足夠的兵力：郡兵能守住城，卻清不空鄉野；地方能彈壓一時，卻無法斷掉糧源與兵源。真正被這場起義改變的，是隋朝分配力量的方式——把主力壓在遼東，就等於把江淮交給地方，這一取捨在往後兩年裡被放大到無法收拾。彭孝才們也給了劉元進、陳瑱、杜伏威等人示範：鄉里武裝只要找到一個縣城、一處山區或一段水路，就可以立旗自保，不必等待中央的召喚。從大業九年的彭城到大業十四年的江都，隋廷的崩解並非一夜之間完成，起義的第一批人只是把裂縫的位置標了出來。隋亡之後，這些鄉里武裝的殘部有一部分被瓦崗、竇建德、杜伏威等群雄收編，成為唐初收拾北方局面的軍事資本。
impactEn: Taken alone, Peng Xiaocai's rising was crushed within the year, was limited in scale, and changed the ownership of no regime; placed within the general picture of the end of the Sui, however, it was the first mark on the pressure gauge. The risings recorded in that year reached across Shandong, Hebei, Henan, the Jiangnan and the southeast, and the county troops of the dynasty were pulled in a dozen directions at once, with the result that not one direction received enough men. The county troops could hold a city but could not clear the countryside; the authorities could suppress a rising for a season but could not cut off its supply of grain or its supply of recruits. What the rising really changed was the way the Sui redistributed its strength: to commit the main body to Liaodong was to hand the Huai region over to the localities, and that choice was magnified over the next two years until it could no longer be taken back. Peng Xiaocai and his men also gave Liu Yuanjin, Chen Zhen and Du Fuwei a demonstration: a local armed band only had to find a county seat, a hill district or a stretch of water in order to raise its flag and hold it, without waiting for any summons from the centre. From Pengcheng in the ninth year of Daye to Jiangdu in the fourteenth, the Sui did not collapse in a single night; the first generation of rebels merely marked where the crack was. After the fall of the Sui, fragments of these local armed bands were absorbed by the contenders — Wolang, Dou Jiande, Du Fuwei — and became the military capital that settled the northern situation in the early Tang.
result: 結局並不光彩：彭孝才這支起義在隋軍的郡兵與臨時調發的援軍到達之後被鎮壓，人眾散去，隊伍退回鄉里或者散為流寇，後來在大業末年隋末群雄的混戰裡再沒有以本名出現的完整建制。史籍沒有記下彭孝才本人的下場，沒有記他是被擒、被殺，還是僥倖脫身；正史對他的最後一筆，就是大業九年彭城起兵這一句，比劉元進、陳瑱、郝孝德等人留下的篇幅都短。可以確定的結果有幾項：其一，隋廷在江淮的鎮壓成功，也就是說這場衝突在軍事上以隋朝獲勝告終；其二，隋朝為此付出的代價，是從遼東調回、從洛陽西線抽調的一批本已捉襟見肘的兵馬，鎮壓地方叛亂與對高句麗作戰從此互相爭奪同一批人；其三，彭孝才之後的江淮起義者不再等待官軍上門，而是把根據地移入山區與水網，把起兵於郡城改成割據於鄉里。對這件卡面兵器而言，羅馬短劍在這場戰役裡沒有出現過一次；真正在此地決定生死的，是刀在貼身距離上怎麼捅出去——這正是環首刀在泗水城牆下要回答的問題。史書缺載，並不表示事情簡單。
resultEn: The ending was not a good one. Once the county troops of the Sui and the reinforcements hastily dispatched to them reached Pengcheng, the rising was crushed; the crowd dispersed, the columns fell back into the villages or dissolved into roving bands, and no complete formation under that name reappeared in the wars that ended the Sui. The histories do not record the fate of Peng Xiaocai himself, whether he was taken, killed or escaped; his last entry in the official record is the single clause that he rose at Pengcheng in the ninth year of Daye, shorter than the notices left by Liu Yuanjin, Chen Zhen and Hao Xiaode. Several outcomes can be stated with certainty. First, the suppression succeeded in the Huai and Yangtze region, which is to say that militarily the conflict ended in a victory for the Sui. Second, the dynasty paid for it with troops drawn back from Liaodong and stripped from the western front at Luoyang, troops who were already stretched to the limit, and from this point on the suppression of local rebellions and the war against Goguryeo competed for the same men. Third, the insurgents of the Huai region who came after Peng Xiaocai no longer waited for the government to come to them, but moved their bases into the hills and the marsh country, changing the formula from rising at the commandery seat to holding the countryside. As for the weapon on the card, the Roman gladius never appeared in this engagement a single time; what decided life and death here was how the knife was put in at the distance of a held breath, and that was the very question the ring-pommel sabre had to answer below the walls of the Sishui. The thinness of the record does not mean that the matter was simple.
